queries.hook: The wish to understand what these texts teach, and to find in them something steady to lean on.
queries.diagnose: When life is lived only for what passes, the heart feels empty; meaning is missing when we forget what does not pass.
queries.steady: What passes cannot fill the heart; turning toward what lasts gives each day a quiet purpose.

alternates.speaker: Bhartrihari
alternates.setting: From 'Worship of Shiva': gratitude for a simple life.
alternates.sanskrit: यदेतत्स्वच्छन्दं विहरणमकार्पण्यमशनं सहार्यैः संवासः श्रुतमुपशमैकव्रतफलम् । मनो मन्दस्पन्दं बहिरपि चिरस्यापि विमृशन् न जाने कस्यैष परिणतिरुदारस्य तपसः ॥
alternates.line: Freedom, simple food, good company, learning that brings calm: what did I do to deserve this?
alternates.translation: This freedom to wander at will, food eaten without humiliation, living among noble people, learning whose only fruit is calm, a mind that stirs only gently even when it looks outward for long: I do not know what generous austerity this is the fruit of.
alternates.why: Gratitude for a simple life, and devotion without rivalry between forms of God.

prasang.summary: Devotional verses longing for a quiet life by the Ganga in Shiva's presence, including a famous non-sectarian line that Shiva and Vishnu are one in essence.
prasang.lesson: Gratitude for a simple life, and devotion without rivalry between forms of God.

alternates.speaker: Krishna
alternates.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on why even the fulfilled keep working for the world.
alternates.sanskrit: यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः । आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते ॥
alternates.line: One who is content and delighted in their own self has nothing left to prove.
alternates.translation: But for the person who delights only in the self, is satisfied with the self, and content in the self alone, there is nothing that must be done.
alternates.why: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verse.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
verse.line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
verse.translation: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
verse.why: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.
verse.misuse: Not 'you're alone, so don't ask for help'. Arjuna himself asks for help; this is about not abandoning yourself.

prasang.title: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

verse.meaning: A person must lift themselves up by their own effort and must not let themselves sink. The self is the only friend, and the self is the only enemy. No outside force can do this for you.
verse.for_you: You have already lifted yourself. The self that guided you here is its own best friend.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today where you choose to lift yourself up rather than push down.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on the cycle of offering that sustains the world.
verse.sanskrit: देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः । परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ ॥
verse.line: Nourish one another, and together you'll reach the highest good.
verse.translation: Nourish the gods with this, and may the gods nourish you. Nourishing one another, you will attain the highest good.
verse.why: Life works by give and take; taking only for yourself breaks the cycle.

prasang.title: Why action as offering is needed
prasang.summary: Krishna describes action as offering, the mutual nourishing of humans and gods, and the wrong of taking without giving back.

verse.for_you: You look back with gratitude, and that is its own offering. To hold this peace is to keep the cycle alive, and in that quiet giving you reach the highest good.

verse.line: Janaka and others reached fulfilment through action. Keep working, if only for the good of the world.
verse.translation: Janaka and others attained perfection through action alone. And looking to the welfare of the world, you too should act.
verse.why: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

verse.try_today: Do one small thing for another person today.
verse.scene_line: You sit in quiet retirement while Janaka still moves through the world.

why: acting for the holding together of the world

verse.speaker: Teacher
verse.setting: The most quoted lines of the graduation address.
verse.sanskrit: देवपितृकार्याभ्यां न प्रमदितव्यम् । मातृदेवो भव । पितृदेवो भव । आचार्यदेवो भव । अतिथिदेवो भव ।
verse.line: Treat your mother as divine, your father as divine, your teacher as divine, your guest as divine.
verse.translation: Do not neglect your duties to the gods and the ancestors. Let your mother be a god to you. Let your father be a god to you. Let your teacher be a god to you. Let your guest be a god to you.
verse.why: Truth, right action, gratitude and graceful giving: a whole life in one speech.
verse.misuse: Honouring parents does not mean accepting mistreatment or giving up your own conscience.

prasang.title: The graduation address
prasang.summary: As a student finishes his studies and leaves to start family life, the teacher gives him parting instructions: speak truth, do right, keep learning, honour mother, father, teacher and guest, give with grace. He even tells the student to copy only the teachers' good conduct, and when in doubt to act as thoughtful, gentle people would.
prasang.lesson: Truth, right action, gratitude and graceful giving: a whole life in one speech.

why: the guest and the elder are served as sacred
those who raised and taught you are to be honoured as one honours a deity

verse.speaker: Sampati
verse.setting: The monkeys despair at the ocean; the old vulture Sampati rouses them.
verse.sanskrit: पापिउ जाकर नाम सुमिरहीं। अति अपार भवसागर तरहीं॥ तासु दूत तुम्ह तजि कदराई राम हृदयँ धरि करहु उपाई ॥
verse.line: Drop your timidity. Keep Ram in your heart and find a way.
verse.translation: Even sinners who remember his name cross the boundless ocean of the world. You are his messengers: give up your timidity, keep Ram in your heart and find a way.
verse.try_today: Keep one steady thought in your heart as you move through the day.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the shore of memory, holding Ram in your heart.

why: act with Ram held in the heart

story.title: Bharata's fourteen-year wait ends
story.story_hook: For fourteen years Bharata had counted the days; now a stranger was telling him to stop.
story.summary: Hanuman finds Bharata thin, in bark clothes, still waiting. Hearing Ram is near, Bharata faints with joy: a person who stays alive will find joy, even after a hundred years. He places the sandals back on Ram's feet and hands back the kingdom he kept in trust, now ten times richer.
story.lesson: Faithful waiting is rewarded; return what was entrusted to you, and more.
story.hook_title: Bharata had counted the days for fourteen years, and then Hanuman arrived
story.teaser: Bharata had counted the days for fourteen years, and then Hanuman arrived
story.for_you: You have held your life with care and made it grow. Now that it is returned to you, this gratitude is the completion of your work.

why: What is held in trust is to be grown and returned without claim; that completes a life's purpose.
